newsitem.title: JAPAN: Weaker yen boosts Matsushita unit's first half.
newsitem.headline: Weaker yen boosts Matsushita unit's first half.

text.p: Matsushita-Kotobuki Electronics Industries Ltd, a core member of Japan's Matsushita group, said on Wednesday that it more than tripled its half-year earnings, largely due to the weaker yen.
The company said it enjoyed a half-year parent current profit of 11.52 billion yen ($101 million), up 266 percent on the same period last year.

Matsushita-Kotobuki is 58-percent owned by electronics giant Matsushita Electric Industrial Co Ltd. Its key business is the production and sale of audio visual equipment and nearly 86 percent of its sales in the six-month period to September 30 came from exports.
"There was price competition, but we were helped by the yen's larger-than-expected downswing," the company said.
The yen stood at around 114 to the dollar on Wednesday, compared with about 100 a year ago.
Japanese companies which export products receive more yen for dollar-denominated exports when the yen's value falls against the U.S. currency.
Current profit is pre-tax, including gains and losses made on securities investments and other non-operating activities.
Matsushita-Kotobuki said it was also helped by a rise in sales.
"We tried very hard to develop and introduce attractive products to cope with demand in the multi-media era. And also we devoted all our energies to the launch of new products," it said.
As a result, the firm posted parent sales of 188.03 billion yen ($1.64 billion) against 175.27 billion yen ($1.53 billion) a year earlier.

The company said it expects the upward trend in its earnings to continue at least throughout the current business year, although it said a quick recovery in the Japanese economy was unlikely in the second half of the business year and that severe competition would continue in the market.
It forecast a full-year parent current profit of 25 billion yen ($219 million) against 8.12 billion yen ($71.2 million) last year.
It said it would post a group net profit of 15.50 billion yen ($135 million) for the full year, against 6.73 billion yen ($59.0 million) last year. ($1=114 yen)
